props.gloss_en: Rabbah to the binders of the Exilarch's hoshana: when you bind it, leave a handgrip on it, so that there be no interposition
Rava: whatever is for its beautification does not interpose
Rabbah: one should not take the hoshana with a cloth
for we require a complete taking, and there is none
Rava: taking by means of another thing is called taking
the mishnah: a short hyssop -- one lengthens it with a thread or a spindle, dips and lifts, grasps the hyssop and sprinkles
the mishnah: [the ashes] fell from the tube into the trough -- unfit
by implication: if he dropped them [from the tube] himself -- fit
Rabbah: one should not insert the lulav into the hoshana, lest leaves fall off and interpose
Rava: a species with its own species does not interpose
Rabbah: one should not trim the lulav [while it is] in the hoshana, for shreds remain and interpose
Rava: a species with its own species does not interpose
Rabbah: it is forbidden to smell the mitzva myrtle
it is permitted to smell the mitzva etrog
why? the myrtle stands for its smell; when he set it aside [for the mitzva], he set it aside from smelling
the etrog stands for eating; when he set it aside, he set it aside from eating
Rabbah: a myrtle while attached [to the ground] -- it is permitted to smell it
an etrog while attached -- it is forbidden to smell it
why? the myrtle stands for smelling; if you permit it, he will not come to cut it
the etrog stands for eating; if you permit it, he will come to cut it
Rabbah: the lulav in the right hand and the etrog in the left
why? these are three mitzvot, and this is one mitzva
we bless only 'concerning the taking of the lulav'
since it is the highest of them all
he said to him: since in its species it is the highest of them all
